Meeting header:

- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Recording: Fireflies capture

Summary:
Quick kickoff between Redwood CS/SE/AE and Acacia Works team to hand off security & network info and align pilot scope. Discussed deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), SSO, audit logs, and a short two-week pilot to validate latency and cost. Several doc links promised.

Topics covered:
- Pilot scope and success metrics (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, correctness on sampled prompts)
- Networking and VPC peering requirements
- SSO / SAML configuration and Okta discussion
- Data residency, logs, and retention policies (SOC2/ISO checkpoints)
- Runbook for onramp and staging checklist

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, i'll run the first few mins and intro folks from our side. um Devon, Priya with me.
[00:12] Maya Chen (Acacia - Head of ML): hey, thanks. this time works. we got Olivia and Samir on too.
[00:18] Devon Lee (Redwood SE): hi all, quick hello from me—i'll be doing the tech handoff. want to make sure we cover network, SSO, and the pilot plan.
[00:26] Carlos Ruiz (IT Lead): perfect. our main ask is we need to lock down the VPC details first, so we can get procurement to approve any peering.
[00:34] Ava Martinez: absolutely. goal for today: hand off the security artifacts and align on who does what in first two weeks.
[00:40] Priya Shah (CSM): also want to set expectations on support hours and runbook. we'll do weekly syncs during pilot.
[00:48] Maya Chen: quick note on pilot success metrics — latency is big for us, p95 under 900ms is target, and cost under $0.10 per 1k tokens if possible.
[00:57] Devon Lee: noted. p95 900ms — depends a bit on model choice and sequence lengths. we'll propose a config, maybe quantized variants on dedicated pool if needed.
[01:08] Samir Patel (Platform Eng): can you clarify dedicated vs private? we are leaning private VPC because of inbound rules and data flow.
[01:16] Devon Lee: yeah so — Redwood hosted is our API, fastest to get started. Dedicated is reserved capacity on Redwood infra with tenancy and predictability. Private (VPC) gives you the control: peered subnets or customer-managed hosts. for regulated data you usually pick Private. small note: our "Redwood Dedicate" term in some docs is spelled weird, sorry, docs will be clean.
[01:34] Olivia Park (Security): we need to see SOC2 Type II excerpts, KMS integration details, and whether HSM is supported for key storage.
[01:43] Ava Martinez: we will attach the security pack. SOC2 excerpts and KMS docs included. HSM: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS; HSM integrations are on roadmap, we'll note as a risk if required.
[01:55] Carlos Ruiz: good, also want audit log granularity — per-token level, or request-level?
[02:02] Devon Lee: primarily request-level with metadata, but we can enable richer tracing: per-token telemetry is heavy and usually internal; we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. we'll include the log schema in the pack.
[02:15] Maya Chen: how do we measure model drift and quality regressions during pilot? can console tie alerts to prompt sets?
[02:22] Priya Shah: yes, Redwood Console has eval hooks and you can tie regressions to prompt sets; we'll set up a small eval with your sample prompts for the two-week run.
[02:33] Devon Lee: action on our side: build a baseline eval suite using the 20 prompts you shared. we'll run nightly diffs and flag any regressions.
[02:40] Maya Chen: ok, i'll drop the prompts in the shared drive after the call.
[02:45] Ava Martinez: great. procurement question — any special contract clauses we should expect?
[02:50] Carlos Ruiz: standard data protection okay, but our legal team insists on breach notification SLA and subprocessor list.
[02:56] Ava Martinez: we'll include subprocessor table and standard breach notification language; can share redlines if needed.
[03:04] Samir Patel: network-wise — we need the IP ranges for Redwood egress and the peering contact. do you support AWS Transit Gateway or only VPC peering?
[03:12] Devon Lee: we support both in most regions; Transit Gateway is supported for enterprise customers. we'll provide IP ranges and recommended routes. note: if you want on-prem, that may need extra steps but it's possible.
[03:22] Olivia Park: question on encryption at rest — is it AES-256 by default? are backups encrypted?
[03:27] Devon Lee: yes AES-256 at rest; backups encrypted; customer keys through KMS if you want to manage them.
[03:33] Maya Chen: small nit — latency numbers you quoted, are they from EU region? since we're primarily EU, need regional numbers.
[03:39] Devon Lee: good call. we'll send region-specific perf bench for the models you want to test. for the pilot we'll provision capacity in eu-west-1 if that suits.
[03:48] Ava Martinez: timeline — propose: security pack by 6/11, staging VPC details by 6/12, network walkthrough 6/15, pilot start 6/22. does that work?
[03:57] Carlos Ruiz: works for us, pending procurement paperwork.
[04:02] Priya Shah: i'll set up weekly check-ins thrusdays during pilot — schedule invite after this meeting.
[04:08] Samir Patel: for the private deployment checklist — what's the canonical runbook? is there an agentless option?
[04:15] Devon Lee: we have a runbook that covers SSO, KMS, peering, subnets, firewall rules, and sample docker image for on-prem. agentless is possible via peered VPC + secure forwarder; on-prem agent is optional for lower-latency setups. i'll draft the minimal checklist.
[04:30] Maya Chen: regarding SSO, we use Okta. any special claims we need to send?
[04:35] Ava Martinez: Okta is common; we need metadata, ACS URL, entity ID. we'll send the SAML guide and a sample metadata file.
[04:42] Olivia Park: can you outline who has access to logs inside Redwood? RBAC model?
[04:46] Devon Lee: RBAC: org/seat level. logs accessible to customer admins; Redwood support can be granted time-limited access for debugging. all access is audited.
[04:56] Carlos Ruiz: great. also curious about tokenization and embedding costs if we use embeddings heavily in the pilot.
[05:03] Priya Shah: we have discrete pricing lines for embeddings vs generation; i'll attach the pricing sheet. for pilot we'll give guidance on conservative settings to reduce unit costs.
[05:14] Maya Chen: ok notes on evaluation: i want per-intent accuracy sampled at 200 requests per day during pilot.
[05:20] Devon Lee: we'll instrument that via the eval hooks and provide a daily dashboard.
[05:26] Ava Martinez: any blockers from your side to start the pre-work?
[05:29] Samir Patel: we need the IPs and the SAML metadata; procurement wants subprocessor list.
[05:34] Ava Martinez: noted — will send in the security zip.
[05:37] Maya Chen: one more — do you support deduplication or caching suggestions for long prompt contexts?
[05:43] Devon Lee: yes, Redwood Optimize has cache/ batching suggestions; for long contexts we recommend KV caching and prefix caching. we'll include a config suggestion for your median seq len.
[05:54] Carlos Ruiz: timeline check — if we sign in two weeks, how quickly can you provision dedicated capacity?
[05:59] Ava Martinez: for reserved Dedicated we need a two-week lead to allocate GPUs in eu region; but for pilot we can use hosted or a small private pool sooner.
[06:08] Maya Chen: ok that's fine.
[06:12] Priya Shah: recap of next steps — we'll send security pack, SSO guide, runbook; customer to share VPC CIDRs and the prompt set. network walkthrough 6/15. pilot 6/22 start.
[06:24] Olivia Park: sounds good. will share procurement contact and subprocessor asks.
[06:28] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone — i'll follow up in email with attachments and the calendar invites.
[06:33] Devon Lee: i'll take the runbook action and put a draft in the shared drive.
[06:36] Maya Chen: thanks, talk soon.
